message.content:
Based on my search, I can provide you with comprehensive information about BMI (Body Mass Index) standards used worldwide.

## What is BMI?

BMI is a screening tool that estimates body fat using a person's weight in relation to their height. It's calculated as:
- **Formula**: weight (kg) ÷ height (m)²
- **US customary**: (weight in pounds × 703) ÷ height in inches²

---

## Standard BMI Classifications

### **WHO/International Standard (Most Widely Used)**

| Category | BMI Range (kg/m²) |
|----------|-------------------|
| Underweight | < 18.5 |
| Normal weight | 18.5 – 24.9 |
| Overweight | 25.0 – 29.9 |
| Obesity Class I | 30.0 – 34.9 |
| Obesity Class II | 35.0 – 39.9 |
| Obesity Class III (Severe/Morbid) | ≥ 40.0 |

This standard is used by the **WHO**, **NIH**, **CDC**, and most Western healthcare systems for White, Hispanic, and Black populations.

---

### **Asian-Specific BMI Standards**

Research has shown that Asian populations experience metabolic risks at lower BMI values. The WHO and many Asian health authorities use adjusted thresholds:

| Category | BMI Range (kg/m²) |
|----------|-------------------|
| Underweight | < 18.5 |
| Normal weight | 18.5 – 22.9 |
| Overweight | 23.0 – 24.9 |
| Obesity | ≥ 25.0 |

Countries using these lower thresholds include **Singapore**, **India**, **China**, **Japan**, **South Korea**, and others. For example, Singapore's Health Hub defines:
- Healthy range: 18.5 – 22.9 kg/m²
- Overweight: ≥ 23.0 kg/m²
- Obese: ≥ 27.5 kg/m²

---

### **China's National Standard (WS/T 428-2013)**

| Category | BMI Range (kg/m²) |
|----------|-------------------|
| Underweight (体重过低) | < 18.5 |
| Normal (体重正常) | 18.5 – 23.9 |
| Overweight (超重) | 24.0 – 27.9 |
| Obese (肥胖) | ≥ 28.0 |

China also uses waist circumference to assess **central obesity**:
- Men: ≥ 90 cm
- Women: ≥ 85 cm

---

### **Special Populations**

| Population | Recommended BMI Range |
|------------|----------------------|
| **Elderly (general)** | 20.0 – 26.9 kg/m² |
| **Ages 80+ (China guideline)** | 22.0 – 26.9 kg/m² |
| **Pregnant women** | BMI-specific weight gain ranges |
| **Children/Teens (2-19 years)** | BMI percentiles for age and sex |
| **Athletes/Muscular individuals** | May need alternative assessments |

---

## Important Limitations of BMI

BMI is a **screening tool**, not a diagnostic measure of body fat or health. It doesn't account for:
- **Muscle mass** (athletes may have high BMI with low body fat)
- **Fat distribution** (visceral vs. subcutaneous fat)
- **Bone density**
- **Age, sex, and ethnicity differences**
- **Overall fitness level**

Healthcare providers increasingly recommend combining BMI with:
- **Waist circumference** (measures abdominal/visceral fat)
- **Body fat percentage**
- **Other metabolic markers** (blood pressure, cholesterol, blood glucose)

---

## Recent Updates and Trends

The WHO has been working on updated classifications that incorporate population-specific cutoffs and complementary metrics. Some sources indicate moves toward:
- Lower thresholds for Asian adults
- Higher healthy ranges for seniors
- Mandatory pairing of BMI with waist circumference and body fat percentage for obesity diagnosis

---

## Clinical Applications

BMI thresholds are commonly used for:
- **Bariatric surgery eligibility**: Typically BMI ≥ 40, or ≥ 35 with comorbidities (some guidelines now include BMI 30-34.9 with metabolic disease)
- **Medication eligibility**: For example, Zepbound (tirzepatide) requires BMI ≥ 30, or ≥ 27 with weight-related conditions
- **Insurance coverage decisions**

---

Sources:
1. https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/articles/9464-body-mass-index-bmi
2. https://www.heart.org/en/healthy-living/healthy-eating/losing-weight/bmi-in-adults
3. https://www.myheart.org.sg/tools-resources/bmi-calculator/
4. https://www.uptodate.com/contents/image?imageKey=OBGYN%2F97661
5. http://www.nhc.gov.cn/ylyjs/s3573d/202412/4cf1905d32304c15ac3bc4446ddb83f1/files/f932c5c0004f4959b92613dd1024483c.pdf
6. http://dayi.org.cn/qa/279026
7. https://www.chinacdc.cn/jkkp/mxfcrb/lnjk/202408/t20240823_295135.html
8. https://www.cdc.gov/bmi/adult-calculator/bmi-categories.html
9. https://apps.who.int/nutrition/landscape/help.aspx?menu=0&helpid=420
10. https://www.boltpharmacy.co.uk/guide/low-bmi-gastric-sleeve
11. https://www.trimbodymd.com/faqs/zepbound-bmi-requirements/
12. https://bmicalculatorweb.com/blog/who-new-bmi-classification-obesity-diagnosis-criteria.html
13. https://carelyclinic.com/gastric-sleeve-eligibility-criteria/
